brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.evidence: 7 full bases at level 0: centre (0,0) plus its six neighbours, in a hexagonal flower layout.
7 top covers, one on every base (cover:*;full;top), all at the same height so they form one flat top.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: 18 caps, one on each of the 18 outside edges the configurator offered (3 per outer cell). No outside edge is left open.

finish.summary:
I built the seven-cell honeycomb work surface: a centre cell with six cells around it, a cover on top of every cell, and caps on all 18 outside edges. The final check passed with no issues, and the collision check came back clear.

I also added one thing you didn't ask for: six joint bolts joining the centre cell to each of its six neighbours. Without them, the check warned that the cells could slide apart. That brings the build to 38 parts.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
